messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a cluster-wide flurry of ECC/Xid alerts in us-west-2 this morning. Looks like short bursts on multiple cards (30s-2m) rather than sustained per-card failures. Can we tune DCGM/Prom rules to avoid noisy drains? cc @jon @lia :wave:
jon: Do we have correlation with reboots/kernel updates? Or perf jobs that spike GPU utilization?
lia: I checked exporter logs — high-cardinality spikes in dcgm_gpu_ecc_errors_total from many pods, then quiet. Mostly Xid 13/31. No coordinated node reboots in the window.
akshay: Current rule is basically alert if increase(...[5m]) > 0 per device, which is catching these microbursts. We should avoid draining on single short bursts.
maria: Agreed. We want to distinguish transient noise vs sustained degradation. Suggesting: require both a higher increase threshold and a "for" window, and prefer recording rules for burst-rate.
lia: Proposed quick rule tweak (untested):
```yaml
groups:
- name: gpu-health
  rules:
  - alert: GPU_ECC_SustainedErrors
    expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_errors_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[10m]) > 5
    for: 15m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "Sustained ECC errors on {{ $labels.instance }} ({{ $labels.gpu_id }})"
```
akshay: Nice. Also add a suppression for recently-rebooted nodes, e.g. require absent_over_time(node_reboot_time[1h]) or exclude label rebooted_recently=1. Prevents paging during kernel/driver rollouts.
maria: +1. Another idea: record a metric for burst intensity so we can threshold on rate, not absolute counts: gpu_ecc_burst_rate = increase(...)/10 then alert when that rate > 0.5 for > 20m. Easier to tune per fleet.
lia: For auto-drain policy, change orchestration to only trigger drains when (1) sustained alert fired AND (2) node-level health shows memory ECC corrected+uncorrected errors above a repair threshold, or when the same GPU hits the alert across 3 different 1h windows.
jon: Operational notes: update alertmanager grouping to coalesce cards by node and not flood on per-gpu labels; route severity=page to paging policy, and add a suppression route for maintenance window label.
maria: I'll draft the PromRule and AM config patch. Also propose a nightly job that runs a cheap scan to mark cards with repeated short bursts (e.g., 3 bursts in 24h) into a review queue instead of auto-replacing — reduces churn.
akshay: Runbook link for reference: https://wiki.redwood.ai/sre/gpu-health-triage (draft). Add a field in node metadata 'ephemeral_flake=true' for cards flagged by sweep so infra team can prioritize replacement in bulk.
lia: Quick follow-ups: (a) can we emit a debug metric from dcgm-exporter for "burst_count" to avoid heavy queries? (b) add a Grafana panel for burst windows so PMs can see noise patterns.
maria: I'll schedule a short rollout: change rule to the 10m/15m for on-call-only for 24h, monitor > reduce false positives, then promote to 30d. Patch will include the recording rule and Alertmanager grouping changes.
deploy-bot: Deployment queued: prometheus-rules/gpu-health v2026.03.18-beta -> canary (1/5 clusters).
jon: Thanks — please ping here after canary results. If noise persists we may need exporter-side smoothing or a small edge cache to collapse microbursts before scrapes. :mag:
